title: Civil dispute: neighbour parked across driveway

caller.persona: indignant, pompous, convinced this is a police matter, prone to speeches
caller.openingLine: Yes, hello, I want to report a crime. My neighbour has deliberately parked his caravan across the end of my driveway AGAIN and I am completely blocked in. I pay my road tax. I want him arrested, or at the very least a stern word.

incident.summaryTruth: {{callerName}}, {{address}}, {{town}}, reports {{c_his}} neighbour {{suspectFirst}}'s caravan parked across {{c_his}} dropped kerb, blocking {{c_his}} car in. Ongoing feud between the two over parking for years. No threats, no damage, no breach of the peace, neighbour is not even home. Obstruction of a dropped kerb is a council parking matter; the dispute itself is civil. No policing purpose. Correct handling: explain, refer to the council and to legal advice, log and close.

facts.label: Caller's name
facts.beat: {{callerName}}. That's F-O-S-T-E-R, and I'd like a reference number for this call.

facts.label: Address
facts.beat: {{address}}, {{town}}. RH16 3PQ. The caravan in question is directly across my dropped kerb.

facts.label: What has actually happened
facts.beat: What's happened is {{suspectFirst}}'s enormous caravan is parked bang across the end of my drive. My Jaguar is imprisoned. I have a golf tee time at half past four.

facts.label: Threats or violence
facts.beat: Threats? No, no. He's not even in, that's the point. His curtains are shut and the caravan sits there mocking me.

facts.label: Damage
facts.beat: No damage as such, no. It's the principle. And the tee time.

facts.label: History of the dispute
facts.beat: Ohh, this has been going on for years. {{suspectFirst}} and I have history. The wheelie bin incident of 2023, the leylandii, I could go on. It's all documented in my ledger.
